topic: GRID10 put into actual sustained operation + a genuinely complex world-model simulation, per Gabriel's explicit request (not just re-running the earlier one-shot acceptance test)

what_was_done.1_finished_building: Ran the existing, already-proven GRID10 acceptance harness (tools/run_grid10_physical_acceptance_v1.py) once more as a fresh baseline (17/17 criteria pass, confirmed live not stale) BEFORE changing anything.
what_was_done.2_built_a_real_multi_tick_world_model: New driver tools/run_grid10_world_model_simulation_v1.py (script name kept v1 for the file, internal schema GRID10_WORLD_MODEL_SIMULATION/v2 -- see honest_scope_statement inside the receipt for why there are two internal draft versions). Reuses the SAME proven grid10_fabric.py/grid10_node.py, but drives a materially richer task graph than the acceptance test: 5 regional/domain scopes + GLOBAL, 6 evidence ticks, a Hyperposition collapse/preserve question per scope, and a real tick-over-tick GWT broadcast/uptake cycle (rotating coordinator each tick, next tick's prompts explicitly reference the prior broadcast).
what_was_done.3_found_and_fixed_a_real_bug_during_actu: The original acceptance test never ran long enough to hit this: a dynamic coordinator's lease enforces an 8-second TTL from its ORIGINAL grant time with no renewal path. Any coordination lasting longer than 8s per scope silently stopped committing forever (the DB's valid=1 flag stays set; only the runtime TTL check inside coordinator_commit fails) -- the coordinator kept polling/looping and reporting healthy, but every packet after the first ~8s just piled up unconsumed in the outbox. Verified directly (110 total packets across 5 scopes across the first 6-tick run, only 5 -- one per scope -- ever committed). Fixed in tools/grid10_node.py: on seeing a commit_error, the coordinator now revokes its own stale lease and re-elects on the next iteration. Verified fix with a real regression test (tests/test_grid10_node_lease_renewal_v1.py, fails against the pre-fix code, passes after) AND empirically re-ran both the acceptance test (still 17/17) and the world-model simulation (all 5 scopes now correctly track evidence across all 6 ticks).
what_was_done.4_found_and_fixed_a_second_bug_in_my_own: First draft of the world-model driver had its own bug: evidence-strength classification used substring matching, so 'confirmed' matched inside 'unconfirmed' and inside 'neither confirmed' (the literal opposite of confirming evidence), and the collapse rule never actually checked whether multiple STRONG-evidence items agreed on the same alternative despite a code comment claiming it did. Caught this during review before reporting results, not after. Rewrote with explicit hand-authored (strength, supports_alternative) triples per evidence item and a corrected agreement check.
what_was_done.5_actually_put_it_into_operation: The first two full runs (v1-buggy and v2-fixed) both completed and exited once their bounded iteration budget ran out -- confirmed this does NOT satisfy 'in Betrieb' (checked minutes later: 0 processes running). Relaunched a third time with a much larger iteration budget (20,000 iterations vs the ~360 used for a single 6-tick demo, ~50 minutes of real wall-clock capacity) so the fabric and all 10 node processes are GENUINELY still running, not just at the moment the driver's own summary was written. Verified this directly via a live process check AFTER the full 6-tick evidence sequence had already completed: 10 node processes (PIDs recorded in the receipt) still alive and polling.
what_was_done.6_external_analysis: ChatGPT bridge reported 'eingeloggt: true / bereit' but the actual send attempt failed for real (403 on the project URL, input-field text mismatch, FAILED_TYPE) -- not something the bridge's own automatic crash-recovery pattern catches (that only triggers on the '0 tabs' signature). nemotron_critique_full_text: The system is a sophisticated coordination protocol, not genuine emergent world-modeling. It maintains a distributed state machine where each tick's GWT broadcast simply shares the latest coordinator summary; the language model only greedy-completes prompts, so no internal model is updated or refined. What's missing for a true world model: (1) a learnable, updatable representation that integrates evidence over time (e.g. neural weights updated via prediction error), (2) counterfactual or predictive simulation capabilities to imagine unseen states, (3) mechanisms for model revision when branches collapse (belief updating, uncertainty propagation), and (4) grounding to real sensorimotor data beyond symbolic audits. The biggest untested weakness is fault tolerance beyond the lease: if a coordinator crashes or the WAL becomes corrupted, there is no recovery protocol to reconstruct the global state or to re-elect a new coordinator without losing pending outbox messages, which could silently corrupt the shared fabric.

my_own_honest_assessment_agreeing_and_ex.agree: Nemotron is right that this is coordination infrastructure, not a world model in any meaningful sense -- the small model contributes only short greedy completions per task; ALL of the actual 'world state' (evidence strength, direction, collapse/preserve decisions) is computed by the DRIVER script from hand-authored ground truth, not learned or inferred by the model. Calling this a 'world model' is generous marketing for what is really 'a distributed state machine with a language-model-flavored logging call attached to each transition.'
my_own_honest_assessment_agreeing_and_ex.extend: Nemotron's crash-recovery point is real but not the ONLY gap I'd flag: (a) the fix I made addresses graceful lease EXPIRY, not a hard coordinator CRASH mid-commit -- Nemotron's WAL-corruption/lost-outbox-message scenario is a genuinely different, harder failure mode I did not test; (b) the Hyperposition rule itself (collapse iff STRONG evidence exists and all STRONG evidence agrees) is my own hand-coded heuristic applied ex post to a scripted evidence sequence I wrote myself -- I have NOT tested what happens with genuinely conflicting STRONG evidence (the code path exists per the v2 fix but was never exercised in this run's evidence script, so it's implemented-but-unverified, not proven); (c) node count (10) and tick count (6) were both chosen for tractability on CPU-only inference, not because they represent any meaningful complexity ceiling -- 'as complex as reasonably possible in the available time' was the real constraint, not 'as complex as the architecture supports'.

current_operational_state_at_time_of_wri.confirmed_how: live 'ps aux' check inside the clay-direct-dev container, performed AFTER the 6-tick evidence sequence had already finished writing its summary -- not just trusting the driver's own end-of-run snapshot

current_operational_state_at_time_of_wri.caveat: This bound was a deliberate, disclosed choice given the CPU-only sandbox and session time constraints, not an attempt to quietly under-deliver on 'in Betrieb' -- flagged explicitly rather than left implicit.
